content: In 1 Timothy, what does Paul call Timothy?
options: My true child in the faith
explanation: Paul was like a spiritual father. “To Timothy, my true child in the faith” (1 Timothy 1:2, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, Paul tells Timothy not to let anyone despise his what?
explanation: Young people can set an example. “Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers” (1 Timothy 4:12, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, why does Paul say Christ Jesus came into the world?
explanation: Paul called himself the worst. “Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst.” (1 Timothy 1:15, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, what is called a root of all kinds of evil?
explanation: Craving it leads people astray. “For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil.” (1 Timothy 6:10, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, godliness with contentment is what?
explanation: We brought nothing into the world. “Of course, godliness with contentment is great gain.” (1 Timothy 6:6, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, Paul tells Timothy to fight the good fight of what?
explanation: Take hold of eternal life. “Fight the good fight of the faith.” (1 Timothy 6:12, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, who is the one mediator between God and men?
explanation: There is one God and one mediator. “and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus” (1 Timothy 2:5, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, physical exercise has some value, but what is valuable in every way?
explanation: It holds promise for this life and the next. “but godliness is valuable in every way” (1 Timothy 4:8, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, what did we bring into the world?
explanation: We cannot carry anything out. “For we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it.” (1 Timothy 6:7, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, with what two things should we be content?
explanation: Contentment is great gain. “But if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these.” (1 Timothy 6:8, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, a person who wants to be an overseer desires what?
explanation: Church leadership is good work. “If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.” (1 Timothy 3:1, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, in which city did Paul urge Timothy to stay?
explanation: To stop false teaching. “you should stay on at Ephesus to instruct certain men not to teach false doctrines” (1 Timothy 1:3, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, what did Paul advise Timothy to use because of his stomach?
explanation: He had frequent ailments. “Stop drinking only water and use a little wine instead, because of your stomach” (1 Timothy 5:23, BSB)

content: In 1 Timothy, in which areas should young Timothy set an example?
explanation: Youth is no excuse. “set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.” (1 Timothy 4:12, BSB)
